propositions.statement: For any DEM cell with finite elevation gradient, the slope magnitude is non-negative.
The slope magnitude of a constant-elevation surface is identically zero everywhere.
Aspect is defined modulo 360 degrees and is undefined only where the gradient vanishes.
For an east-facing planar slope, the computed aspect equals 90 degrees under the cartographic convention.
Profile curvature is non-negative at a local elevation maximum of a smooth DEM.
Plan (tangential) curvature is non-negative at a local elevation minimum of a smooth DEM.
For a quadratic bump h = A - k*(x^2+y^2), the profile curvature at the apex equals -2k up to a sign convention.
Hillshade lies in [0,255] for any finite slope and any azimuth/altitude in their domains.
Hillshade of a flat surface equals 255 * sin(altitude) under the standard Horn shading model.
D8 flow direction at a local pit points to no downslope neighbor (undefined / no-flow).
On a uniform planar slope the D8 flow direction is constant across all interior cells.
If point B is visible from A, then A is visible from B only when the line of sight is unobstructed in both directions (symmetry under mutual obstruction).
Visibility is a reflexive relation only on the diagonal; for distinct points it is not guaranteed symmetric.
A closed contour encloses a region whose interior elevation is either entirely above or entirely below the contour level.
Every interior cell belongs to exactly one watershed basin under a deterministic flow-routing rule.
Topographic Position Index is zero on a planar (constant-curvature) surface.
Terrain Ruggedness Index is non-negative and zero on a planar surface.
Bilinear resampling of a planar surface at a coarser resolution preserves the plane (no introduced curvature).
The Horn (1981) finite-difference slope operator is a consistent estimator of the analytic slope as the grid spacing tends to zero.
The discrete profile-curvature operator converges to the analytic profile curvature of a C^2 surface in the limit of vanishing grid spacing.
